items.headline: Singapore unveils OTC gold-clearing system and central-bank gold vaulting
items.summary: At the 9th Asia-Pacific Precious Metals Conference on June 15, Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong said SGX will run a new over-the-counter gold-clearing system for Loco Singapore by end-2026 with six clearing banks, including DBS, OCBC, UOB and JPMorgan, while MAS will launch central-bank gold vaulting services by October.

items.headline: Sushil Sukumaran Nair appointed a Justice of Singapore's Court of Appeal
items.summary: Singapore appointed Justice Sushil Sukumaran Nair, a veteran restructuring lawyer and former Drew & Napier deputy chief executive, as a Justice of the Court of Appeal with effect from June 15.

items.headline: Most Singapore fresh graduates earn below their expected pay, MOM study finds
items.summary: A Ministry of Manpower School-to-Work Transition Study found fresh graduates across most fields earned less than they expected - information-technology graduates anticipated about S$6,000 a month but earned around S$5,150 - and that 30.6 per cent of those who turned down a job offer cited low pay.

items.headline: Man, 28, jailed 8 years 9 months and caned for raping girl, 13, he met online
items.summary: Kevin Tan Jia Hut, 28, was sentenced to eight years and nine months' jail and six strokes of the cane after pleading guilty to raping a 13-year-old girl he had met online in 2023.

items.headline: India's May trade deficit widens to $28.21 billion as record exports lag imports
items.summary: Commerce Ministry data released June 15 showed merchandise exports rose 18 per cent year-on-year to a record $45.2 billion in May, but imports climbed 20.6 per cent to $73.41 billion, widening the merchandise trade deficit to $28.21 billion.

items.headline: AAIB's final report on Air India AI-171 crash to come 'very soon', says minister
items.summary: Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu said on June 15 that the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau's final report on the June 2025 Air India AI-171 crash, which killed 260 people in Ahmedabad, would be released 'very soon' but would follow international protocols and not be rushed.

items.headline: Sensex jumps 736 points and the rupee firms as US-Iran deal sinks oil
items.summary: India's Sensex closed up 736 points (0.97 per cent) at 76,264 and the Nifty 50 added 231 points to 23,854 on June 15, while the rupee strengthened, after the United States and Iran announced a deal to end their war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

items.headline: Modi begins France visit, to join G7 outreach session at Evian
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi began a visit to France on June 15, holding talks with President Emmanuel Macron and preparing to attend the G7 outreach sessions at Evian on June 16-17 - India's 13th participation in the summit - with artificial intelligence, trade and West Asia on the agenda.

items.headline: IMD widens heavy-rain and thunderstorm alerts as monsoon advances across India
items.summary: The India Meteorological Department said the southwest monsoon advanced further into eastern and central India by June 15 and warned of thunderstorms gusting to 70 kmph over Rajasthan and heavy rain over Tamil Nadu and Karnataka on June 16-17.

items.headline: Update: Trump says ships are moving through Hormuz as US-Iran signing set for Friday
items.summary: President Trump said on June 15 that ships were 'starting to move' through the Strait of Hormuz and that a formal US-Iran deal to end the war would be signed Friday in Switzerland; US officials said a memorandum had already been agreed, though the full text has yet to be released and Vice-President JD Vance will attend the signing.

items.headline: Russian strike sets historic Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra cathedral ablaze, killing at least 5
items.summary: A large overnight Russian barrage of more than 60 missiles and drones hit Kyiv on June 15, killing at least five people and igniting a fire on the roof of the main cathedral at the UNESCO-listed Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra; rescuers were also killed by a second strike in Kharkiv, and President Zelensky called it one of Russia's most serious crimes against Christian culture.

items.headline: G7 leaders open Evian summit and welcome the US-Iran deal
items.summary: G7 leaders convened in Evian, France on June 15, with host President Macron calling the US-Iran agreement 'a very important step for peace'; Ukraine, trade and artificial intelligence top the agenda, and President Zelensky was invited to a working session.

items.headline: World Cup debutants Cape Verde hold Spain to a 0-0 draw
items.summary: Cape Verde, playing their first World Cup, held reigning European champions Spain to a 0-0 draw in Atlanta on June 15, with 40-year-old goalkeeper Vozinha saving all seven of Spain's shots on target as Spain managed 27 attempts without scoring.

items.headline: Tunisia sack coach Sabri Lamouchi after 5-1 World Cup loss to Sweden
items.summary: Tunisia dismissed head coach Sabri Lamouchi on June 15 after a 5-1 defeat to Sweden in their World Cup opener in Monterrey, in which Alexander Isak and Viktor Gyokeres scored and Yasin Ayari struck twice from distance; former boss Mondher Kebaier was named interim coach.

items.headline: Salesforce to acquire AI customer-service firm Fin for $3.6 billion
items.summary: Salesforce said on June 15 it had agreed to buy Fin - the customer-support company formerly known as Intercom - for about $3.6 billion, folding Fin's AI support agent into its Agentforce platform; the deal is expected to close in Salesforce's fiscal fourth quarter of 2027.

items.headline: Nvidia sells $25 billion of bonds in its first debt offering since 2021
items.summary: Nvidia priced a $25 billion seven-tranche investment-grade bond sale on June 15, its first since a $5 billion deal in 2021, after orders swelled to about $85 billion; the chipmaker joins a wave of big-tech borrowing to fund the AI build-out.

items.headline: UK to bar under-16s from social media, including TikTok and YouTube
items.summary: Prime Minister Keir Starmer said on June 15 that Britain will ban under-16s from major social-media platforms - including TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Snapchat, Facebook and X - from early 2027, following Australia's model; messaging apps such as WhatsApp and Signal are exempt.

items.headline: SpaceX stock jumps 20% in its first full day of trading after record IPO
items.summary: SpaceX shares rose about 20 per cent on June 15, their first full trading day, after the company's record $75 billion Nasdaq debut on June 12; the gains pushed its market value well above $2 trillion.

items.headline: Update: Bank of Japan set to raise rates to 1% today as Ueda misses meeting
items.summary: The Bank of Japan concludes its two-day meeting on June 16 with markets pricing a near-certain 25-basis-point hike to 1.00 per cent, which would be its highest policy rate since 1995; Governor Kazuo Ueda, hospitalised with an infected liver cyst, is absent, leaving Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino to preside.

items.headline: Nikkei 225 surges about 5% to a record high above 69,000
items.summary: Japan's Nikkei 225 jumped about 5 per cent on June 15 to close at a record high above 69,000 for the first time, lifted by the US-Iran peace deal and positioning before the Bank of Japan's expected rate hike.

items.headline: Wall Street rallies on US-Iran deal as S&P 500 climbs 1.65% and the Dow hits a record
items.summary: US stocks rallied on June 15 after the US-Iran deal, with the S&P 500 rising 1.65 per cent to 7,554 and the Nasdaq up more than 3 per cent, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at a record; oil fell as the agreement cleared the way to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

items.headline: Update: Oil slides further as US-Iran deal clears the way to reopen Hormuz
items.summary: Crude oil fell again on June 15, extending a slide that has taken prices down about 20 per cent from their 2026 war-driven peak, after the United States and Iran agreed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and lift the US blockade of Iranian ports.

items.headline: 🏏 India beat Pakistan by 64 runs at the Women's T20 World Cup
items.summary: India beat Pakistan by 64 runs in Birmingham on June 14 at the Women's T20 World Cup, with Smriti Mandhana making 68 and Deepti Sharma taking 5 for 10 as Pakistan were bowled out for 106 chasing 171.

items.headline: 🏏 Bangladesh beat Netherlands by six wickets on the Dutch World Cup debut
items.summary: Bangladesh beat Netherlands by six wickets in Birmingham on June 14, chasing down 140 with five balls to spare on the Dutch side's Women's T20 World Cup debut; opener Juairiya Ferdous made a half-century on her T20I debut and was named player of the match.

items.headline: 🎾 Tiafoe upsets French Open finalist Cobolli in the Halle first round
items.summary: Frances Tiafoe beat recent French Open finalist Flavio Cobolli 6-2, 7-6(4) in the first round of the grass-court Halle Open on June 15, as second seed Felix Auger-Aliassime also advanced.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli leads the F1 title race by 43 points as the season heads to Austria
items.summary: After winning the Canadian Grand Prix, Kimi Antonelli leads the 2026 Formula 1 standings by 43 points from Mercedes team-mate George Russell, with the next round the Austrian Grand Prix at the Red Bull Ring on June 28.

fun_fact.headline: Wombats produce cube-shaped droppings
fun_fact.body: Wombats are the only known animals that produce cube-shaped droppings. Researchers found the marsupial's intestines have regions of differing stiffness that mould the faeces into roughly cubic pellets, which the animals stack to mark territory without them rolling away. The discovery earned a 2019 Ig Nobel Prize.

puzzle.title: The Painted Cube
puzzle.body:
A wooden cube measuring 4 x 4 x 4 is painted red on all six outer faces, then sliced into 64 unit cubes.
How many of the small cubes have paint on exactly two faces?
puzzle.approach: Picture where on the big cube a small cube must sit to show exactly two painted faces - the edges, not the corners or the centres.
puzzle.answer:
24.
Cubes with exactly two painted faces lie along the edges of the big cube but not at its corners. Each of the 12 edges has 4 - 2 = 2 such cubes, so 12 x 2 = 24. (For reference: 8 corner cubes have three painted faces, 6 x 4 = 24 face-centre cubes have one, and the 8 innermost cubes have none.)
